My Story

From 150kg to Roughly 90kg

I didn't start as a coach. I started as someone who needed to change his relationship with food, training, and his own body — at around 150 kg, carrying weight that affected my energy, my confidence, and my health.

The process wasn't fast, and it wasn't a straight line. What worked was consistency built on fundamentals: eating in a sustainable calorie deficit, prioritizing protein, training with resistance three to five times a week, and protecting sleep and recovery. No shortcuts, no extreme protocols — just the basics, applied for long enough to matter.

Over time, that process took me down to approximately 90 kg. Alongside it, I kept studying — I'm currently a clinical pharmacy student — which pushed me to understand the "why" behind every part of the process, not just the "what."

That's the coaching I offer now: the same principles that worked for me, adapted to your body, your schedule, and your goals.

— Ahmed

Coaching Services

Choose the path that matches your goal

Every program is built around your starting point — not a template. Here's where most clients begin.

01

Fat Loss

A structured calorie deficit paired with resistance training and daily activity targets, designed to preserve muscle while body fat comes down — sustainably, without crash dieting.

02

Body Recomposition

For clients who want to lose fat and build muscle at the same time. Nutrition and training are balanced carefully around maintenance, with progression tracked closely.

03

Muscle Building & Strength

A structured hypertrophy and strength program with progressive overload, built around a calorie surplus or maintenance intake and a training split suited to your schedule.

How It Works

Science-Based Approach

Built on fundamentals that hold up

Calories

Your intake is set relative to your maintenance level, based on your goal — not a generic number pulled from an app.

Macros

Protein, carbohydrate, and fat targets are set to support training performance, recovery, and body composition goals.

Resistance Training

A structured program is the foundation for preserving and building muscle, whatever the goal — fat loss included.

Progressive Overload

Training load, volume, or difficulty increases over time in a planned way, so your body keeps adapting.

Sleep & Recovery

Recovery is treated as part of the program, not an afterthought — it directly affects performance, hunger, and results.

Goal Setting

There's no universal "ideal weight"

Your ideal weight isn't a number pulled from a chart — it depends on you specifically.

  • Height and frame size
  • Body composition — muscle mass versus fat mass, not just the scale
  • Current health status and any medical considerations
  • Your personal goals: performance, aesthetics, long-term health, or all three

In our consultation, we set a goal that's realistic and specific to your body and life — not a borrowed target.

About Ahmed

A student of pharmacy. A student of his own body.

I'm a third-year clinical pharmacy student with a personal transformation from roughly 150 kg to 90 kg. That experience — combined with ongoing, practical self-education in training and nutrition — is the foundation of how I coach.

I coach based on real, applied experience and continuous learning of evidence-based fitness and nutrition principles. I'm not a licensed physician, dietitian, or clinical nutritionist, and coaching does not replace medical care — clients with underlying health conditions are encouraged to coordinate with their doctor alongside our work together.
